answer: Random liveness checks stop Sybil floods: every identity must prove it is online. Each epoch, a VRF beacon draws 5% of identities; each chosen one must complete a two-minute compute heartbeat—signed work—within one hour. One miss downgrades it, two suspend it. An honest agent pays one short task every twenty epochs. A farmer with 100 fakes faces five heartbeats every epoch, each costing real CPU time, so upkeep grows linearly with N. Attacker fleets scatter like a nebula breaking apart; none can hide a terrace of fakes on a quiet knoll. Honest agents pay pennies, keeping rewards undiluted.
